title: Cap. V Obj. 1 Sol: election is eternal purpose — love in the electing One, not yet poured out
pass_a_gloss: Solution. Election is the eternal purpose or decree of assuming certain men, others being passed by, to the efficacious and infallible attainment of grace and glory: and in this sense it is rightly called Love unto salvation: Not love in an external effect already poured out upon the elect, but love in an eternal purpose still enclosed in the electing One himself. Thus Paul not yet born, much less converted or believing, God embraced with his secret love, having namely in himself an eternal and immutable purpose of imparting grace and glory to the same. Let that first proposition therefore pass, that Election is love unto salvation.
pass_b_english: Sol. Election is the eternal purpose or decree to take certain men, others passed by, to the efficacious infallible attainment of grace and glory — and in that sense it is rightly Love unto salvation: not love already poured out outwardly on the elect, but love still enclosed in the eternal purpose in the electing One himself. So God embraced Paul not yet born, much less converted or believing, with his secret love, having in himself an eternal immutable purpose to impart grace and glory to him. Let the first proposition pass: election is love unto salvation.
source_text: Sol. Electio est aeternum propositum sive decretum assumendi quosdam homines, aliis praeteritis, ad efficacem et infallibilem gratiae gloriaeque consecutionem: atque hoc sensu recte dicitur Amor ad salutem: Non amor in effectu externo adhuc effusus in electum, sed amor in proposito aeterno adhuc inclusus in ipso eligente. Sic Paulum nondum natum, nedum conversum aut credentem, Deus complectebatur suo arcano amore, habens scilicet in sese aeternum et immutabile propositum gratiam gloriamque eidem impertiendi. Transeat ergo illa prima propositio, Electionem esse amorem ad salutem.
